newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA STATE INSURER MOVES TO COMBAT RAMPANT FRAUD.
newsitem.headline: CHINA STATE INSURER MOVES TO COMBAT RAMPANT FRAUD.

text.p: Rampant insurance fraud is costing the People's Insurance Company of China (PICC) Property large sums of money and forcing the state-run giant to tighten its underwriting process, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
"Insurance fraud has risen dramatically in recent years, cost the company a huge amount of money annually and slowed payments to honest claimants," the newspaper quoted a company official as saying.
One or two of every 10 motor insurance claims were fraudulent, the newspaper quoted Jia Haimao, deputy manager of PICC Property's motor insurance department, as saying.
"The fraud is particularly prevalent in the vehicle insurance sector, but false claims also are filed against fire and house insurance policies," Jia said.
Jia did not give the total number of motor fraud cases the company had uncovered but said fraudulent claims ranged between 5,000 yuan ($600) and 200,000 yuan.
"Some people bought an insurance policy for an inexpensive vehicle, then burned, blew up or dropped the vehicle off a hillside," he said.
Other vehicle owners bought insurance and then falsely reported their vehicles stolen, he said.
To battle the wave of false claims, PICC Property had been forced to improve its underwriting system and claims investigation, he said.

Underwriters should personally check vehicles carefully before signing policies and should investigate the scenes of accidents, he said. Contracts would also become more detailed to try to prevent loopholes.
The company would disclose details of every compensation case and offer rewards to people who exposed false claims, he said.
PICC Property, China's largest general insurer, had 70 percent of the motor insurance market last year and settled 1.9 million claims, paying out more than 10 billion yuan in compensation, it said.
The company's premiums in 1996 totalled 35 billion yuan, of which 21 billion yuan came from motor insurance.
-- Beijing Newsroom (86-10) 6532-1921 Sunday, 27 July 1997 07:01:27 ENDS nPEK01663
